title: 29.2 A 0.021μm2 High-Density SRAM in Intel-18A-RibbonFET Technology with PowerVia-Backside Power Delivery
problem: Advancing to sub-2nm nodes requires higher density and lower V_MIN (minimum operating voltage) to maintain power efficiency; FinFET bitcell scaling limits are reached; traditional frontend power distribution uses valuable signal routing tracks.
motivation: AI accelerators and HPC systems demand exponentially larger on-chip memory at lower power; RibbonFET technology enables better P/W and improved density vs. FinFET; backside power delivery (PowerVia) frees frontend routing for signal interconnects.
method: The design uses a standard 6-transistor memory cell built with Intel's new RibbonFET transistors (ultra-thin transistors that wrap around a silicon fin) with adjustable widths to fine-tune performance. Power delivery moves to the back of the chip (PowerVia) instead of routing through the front, reducing power supply noise (voltage droop) that normally forces higher operating voltages. By redesigning the core memory cell and its surrounding circuits together, they fit more memory into the same space while maintaining a low minimum operating voltage, without needing extra circuit assist features.
key_novelty: The core innovation is combining backside power delivery (PowerVia) with RibbonFET transistors to eliminate voltage droop, achieving a record 38.1 megabits per square millimeter of memory density while reducing the minimum operating voltage and eliminating the need for assist circuits.
contributions: 0.77x bitcell area scaling vs. FinFET for high-current (HCC) variant
0.88x bitcell area scaling vs. FinFET for high-density (HDC) variant
34.3 Mb/mm^2 HDC array with write assist (68mV V_MIN improvement)
Up to 38.1 Mb/mm^2 with larger bit array and peripheral compaction
Improved V_MIN without read assist vs. prior FinFET designs
PowerVia enables efficient peripheral circuit design with freed frontside routing
baselines: FinFET-based SRAM (7nm, larger bitcells, higher V_MIN)
limitations: Abstract does not provide access time, power consumption per access, leakage current, or yield/reliability data. Scaling to future nodes beyond 18A not discussed.
primary_theme: Ultra-dense RibbonFET SRAM with backside power delivery
